overview: Chipotle's fiscal Q2 2026 revenue rose 9.3% to $3.3B, with comparable restaurant sales up 2.2% including a 1% transaction comp, versus 0.5% in Q1. Restaurant level margin was 25.2%, down 220bp, and adjusted diluted EPS was $0.33, flat y/y. Adam Rymer, CFO, guided full-year comps to the low single digits and Q3 comps to around plus 1%, assuming a roughly 200bp Cyclospora-related softness persists.
keyTakeaways: Adam Rymer, CFO, said traffic improved through Q2 and into early July, then softened by about 200bp in the second half of July around the industry Cyclospora issue.
Scott Boatwright, CEO, said Chipotle is not involved in the Cyclospora conversation and is affected on sales only, since the implicated products are not on the menu.
Boatwright said HEAP gives two to four hours of labor efficiency, will be in 2,000 restaurants by year-end, and should cover the whole portfolio sometime in 2027.
Boatwright said the affordability scores were better in Q2 than in probably the past couple of years, and the younger and lower-income cohorts improved the most, per Rymer.
Boatwright said a frictionless in-restaurant rewards pilot begins in August, since only about 20% of in-restaurant transactions scan versus nearly 90% of digital.
financialHighlights: Revenue was $3.3B, up 9.3%, with comparable restaurant sales up 2.2% and pricing impact of about 1.6%.
Restaurant level margin was 25.2%, down 220bp y/y, with cost of sales at 29.7% (up about 80bp), labor at 25.0% (up about 30bp) and other operating costs at 14.9% (up about 90bp).
Digital sales were $1.3B, or 38.3% of sales versus 35.5% a year ago.
Adjusted diluted EPS was $0.33, flat y/y, with non-GAAP G&A of $176M.
Chipotle repurchased $631M of stock at an average $32.55, ended with $800M of cash, restricted cash and investments and no debt, and had $1.7B of authorization remaining after an additional $1.3B.

guidance: Rymer guided full-year comparable restaurant sales growth to the low single-digit range, versus about flat last quarter, and Q3 comps to around plus 1% assuming the roughly 200bp Cyclospora impact persists.
Rymer guided Q3 menu pricing to the mid 2% range and full-year pricing to the high end of 1%-2%, with price matching inflation from Q4.
Rymer guided Q3 cost of sales to just under 30%, labor to the mid 25% range, other operating costs to the mid 15% range and marketing to the low 3% range.
Rymer guided Q3 non-GAAP G&A to around $180M, full-year depreciation to around 3% of sales and the underlying tax rate to 24%-26%.
Boatwright expects about 350 new company-owned openings this year, about 80% with a Chipotlane, and national launch of catering and Build-Your-Own Chipotle in 2027.

qa.question: More color on the low-single-digit comp guide, including Q3 and the recent softening.
qa.answer: Rymer said Q2 traffic improved through the quarter and into the first half of July, then softened by about 200bp in the second half of July. He said Q3 is the toughest lap and comps are expected around plus 1% if the impact continues. Scott Boatwright, CEO, said Chipotle is not involved in the Cyclospora conversation.

qa.question: Where does confidence in momentum into 2027 come from, given tough comparisons, a recent slowdown and 1%-2% comps?
qa.answer: Boatwright said Q2 transaction growth was early days of Recipe for Growth, with proof points in guest satisfaction, food quality and operational consistency. He said menu innovation, rewards engagement, brand communication and group occasions will build through H2 2026 and into 2027.
qa.read: Answered partially: no quantified evidence for 2027.

qa.question: Has the incremental capex and sales uplift from the restaurant remodel or refresh program been sized?
qa.answer: Boatwright said Chipotle has never done an aesthetic remodel and is stage-gating a refresh at several locations at roughly $100,000-$300,000 per restaurant. He said he has nothing to report yet.
qa.read: Answered partially: gave the cost range but no results.

qa.question: With a new CMO, how will the brand be positioned given For Real has gone stale, and will value be highlighted more?
qa.answer: Boatwright said the new work is the next evolution of For Real, with more on fresh preparation and ingredients, and value framed as extraordinary value from best ingredients, not price points or discounts. First elements are visible later this quarter.
qa.read: Answered partially: pushed back on the stale premise and gave no specifics.

qa.question: What could be better in promoting loyalty in restaurant, and do non-loyalty transactions over-index to lower-income guests?
qa.answer: Boatwright said the non-loyalty 20% of in-store transactions are broad-based, not lower-income, and could see meaningful lift if enrolled. He said an August one-stop pay pilot will award points on payment and allow enrollment without relying on the restaurant team.

qa.question: Are the new menu items center-of-the-plate or sides, and any more detail?
qa.answer: Boatwright said the culinary team is working on center-of-the-plate items, beverage, sides and desserts. He said some big ideas could be on the calendar in the back half of 2026 but certainly in 2027.
qa.read: Answered partially: no specific items named.
